findings.problem: MetricWorkflow uses raw primitives (String status, bool is_validated, bool is_sent, Option<u64> sent_at_epoch_ms) instead of enum-based typestates, allowing callers to construct invalid state combinations such as is_validated=true with status="pending" or is_sent=true with status="pending".
findings.failure_mode: Callers can place MetricWorkflow into logically impossible states that are only detectable at runtime; no compile-time guarantee that status, lifecycle booleans, and timestamps are coherent.
findings.fix: Replace status: String with an enum (e.g., enum WorkflowStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent }) and is_validated: bool / is_sent: bool with an enum or typestate that makes illegal combinations unrepresentable. Remove or privatize the raw fields.

findings.problem: All fields are pub raw primitives (String, bool, Option); the struct has no fallible constructor, builder, or parse boundary. Callers can construct invalid states directly without any validation.
findings.failure_mode: Every caller bypasses domain invariants by setting struct fields directly, making it impossible to enforce that status matches lifecycle flags or that sent_at_epoch_ms is Some only when is_sent is true.
findings.fix: Make all fields private, add a fallible smart constructor (e.g., fn new(id: &str) -> Result<MetricWorkflow, MetricError>) and/or use newtyped IDs and enum variants so invalid states are unrepresentable at the type level.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are independent lifecycle flags that can be set to contradictory combinations (e.g., both true, both false, or validated without sent).
findings.failure_mode: Runtime logic depending on these booleans will misbehave under invalid combinations (double-sent, sent-but-not-validated, or validated-but-not-marked-sent).
findings.fix: Replace both booleans with a single enum WorkflowState { Pending, Validated, Sent } or use a typestate pattern with separate types for each lifecycle phase.

findings.problem: status: String allows any arbitrary string value (e.g., "foo", "", "SENT"). mark_sent sets it to "sent" by string literal, which is fragile and not enforced by the type system.
findings.failure_mode: Typos, case mismatches, or unexpected string values break status-dependent logic; no exhaustiveness checking on match arms.
findings.fix: Replace with enum WorkflowStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent } and use pattern matching with exhaustive arms.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive without a domain newtype, making it indistinguishable from other string fields and allowing empty or malformed IDs.
findings.failure_mode: Caller can pass an empty string or malformed ID; no domain-level validation at the type level.
findings.fix: Introduce a newtype: pub struct WorkflowId(String) or use a parse-boundary constructor that validates and rejects empty/malformed IDs.

findings.problem: mark_sent blindly overwrites status to "sent" and sets is_sent=true regardless of prior state (e.g., it does not check if the workflow was already sent or if it was validated first).
findings.failure_mode: Double-send or sending an unvalidated workflow silently succeeds; the function has no precondition checks and no error return.
findings.fix: Refactor mark_sent to take an enum-based state and return Result<MetricWorkflow, MetricError> (or a typestate transition) that enforces valid transitions (e.g., only Pending can transition to Sent, or only Validated can transition to Sent).

findings.problem: MetricWorkflow contains two owned String fields (id, status) and mark_sent performs "sent".to_string() allocation on every call. No allocation analysis or evidence for this pattern.
findings.failure_mode: Repeated mark_sent calls on hot paths cause unnecessary heap allocations; if id is re-settable, it also causes reallocation of the original String.
findings.fix: Use Cow<'static, str> for status, or prefer an enum (which has zero heap allocation). If id must be owned, benchmark to confirm the allocation budget is acceptable.

findings.problem: No benchmarks exist to establish performance baselines for MetricWorkflow or mark_sent.
findings.failure_mode: No evidence that the code meets any performance claim; allocation behavior of String fields is unmeasured.
findings.fix: Add a benchmark (e.g., Criterion) for mark_sent to measure allocation and throughput.

findings.problem: No profiler evidence exists to confirm hot paths or allocation patterns.
findings.failure_mode: Cannot identify whether the String allocations in mark_sent are actually a performance concern.
findings.fix: Run perf or flamegraph on a representative workload to confirm allocation hotspots.

findings.problem: No CLI or second-ring command-layer evidence exists for the MetricWorkflow domain.
findings.failure_mode: The imperative shell boundary is not visible; no evidence of how I/O boundaries are handled.
findings.fix: Add a shell-layer module with explicit I/O that parses at boundaries into the domain type and performs actions.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent throughput or allocation
no profiler evidence for String allocation patterns
no CLI or second-ring command-layer evidence
no allocation budget evidence for owned String fields
residual_risk: The struct has no typestate enforcement and allows all illegal state combinations at the type level. Without enum-based status and lifecycle state machine, the only defense is manual runtime checks which are error-prone. The code also lacks any parse boundary or smart constructor, meaning every caller can violate domain invariants.
